analysis.title: Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) First Take: Slight Earnings Beat Led By Mid-Continent; Announces ~$4 Billion in Refining Asset Sales
key_insights: MPC reported 3Q26 EPS of $26.93 versus GS consensus of $26.50 and FactSet consensus of $25.37. Refining and Midstream, and Renewable Diesel came in stronger than GS segment estimates.

MPC agreed to divest the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries to CVR Energy (CVI) for $4.2 bn. MPC receives $3.45 bn for the refining assets and MPLX receives $750 mn for related midstream assets, a 9x multiple on 2027 EBITDA forecasts. Close is expected at the end of 2026.
Management intends to reinvest the sale proceeds primarily in the Gulf Coast and to support MPLX growth in the Permian and Marcellus basins.

Refining adjusted EBITDA was $9,895 mn versus GS $9,590 mn, driven by Mid-Continent adjusted EBITDA of $4,159 mn versus GS $3,845 mn. West Coast contributed less than modeled and Gulf Coast was in line.

Total throughput was above GS estimates in the Gulf Coast, Mid-Continent and West Coast. Gulf Coast and West Coast gross margins were below GS, at $43.36/bbl vs $44.62 and $47.46/bbl vs $49.57, while Mid-Continent margin was $47.33/bbl vs $46.36.
Midstream adjusted EBITDA was $1,882 mn versus GS $1,792 mn. Renewable Diesel adjusted EBITDA was $254 mn versus GS $234 mn, roughly in line.
4Q26 total throughput guidance is about 3.0 mbpd, in line with the GS estimate of about 3.0 mbpd.
GS keeps a Buy rating with a 6-month price target of $519 (20.6% upside from $430.39), based on 15.0x P/E on normalized EPS and a sum-of-the-parts.
GS forecasts EPS of $63.67 for 2026E, $51.53 for 2027E and $28.28 for 2028E, versus $10.79 in 2025. The 2026E P/E is 6.8x and FCF yield is 14.6%.
GS expects heavy buybacks: share repurchases of $10,281 mn in 2026E and $13,750 mn in 2027E.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 EPS of $26.93 beat GS $26.50, led by Mid-Continent refining. Price target is based on 15.0x normalized EPS and a sum-of-the-parts.
CVR Energy agreed to buy the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries from MPC for $4.2 bn including related midstream assets. The report gives no CVI rating or view.
